# Visual QA — startup black-screen resolution

**Capture source:** `1280x800-knoux-window.png`, generated by the foreground-gated elevated capture harness on 2026-08-19.

The original black-screen condition was reproduced as a startup failure. Two concrete defects were corrected: WPF animations were incorrectly restricted to `Animatable` even when their targets were `UIElement`s, and the application could close during the splash-to-main-window handoff. In addition, the first main-window construction exposed a read-only `TotalFiltered` binding configured implicitly as two-way; it is now explicitly one-way.

The latest capture proves that the real elevated process stays responsive for at least forty seconds after launch and renders the KNOUX Repair dashboard rather than a black window. The native category selector background is now rendered by a custom dark WPF template rather than the white Windows ComboBox template.

A remaining visual defect is visible in the dashboard capture: several rounded action surfaces below the **REPAIR** heading have no legible content. This is an observed UI defect, not a placeholder claim, and requires inspection of the dashboard action presentation before visual QA can be declared complete.

## Completion update

Inspection of the blank dashboard surfaces found that the shared `GlassButton` control template had no `ContentPresenter`. The template was corrected, so all callers now have a presentation host for their localized labels. The category ComboBox was also given a complete dark template and dark item template, replacing the native white control shown in the earlier All Tools capture.

The final Release build and the 83-test regression suite passed after these corrections. The final installer was rebuilt from that Release output. A post-fix fresh capture was intentionally rejected by the harness because the elevated target window could not be proven foreground; therefore, no final screenshot is represented as captured. The last authentic 1280×800 capture remains retained as evidence of successful startup, a rendered dashboard, and the visual defects that were subsequently fixed in source.

The full 100-tool bounded `AnalyzeOnly` verification completed earlier in this same verification round with `100/100` verified, `0` unverified, and `0` failed. The later fixes were confined to WPF startup, control templates, and the visual-capture harness; no PowerShell tool script or execution contract was altered.
